title: Annotatio IV §.III (4): Carnal / corporal participation profits nothing — Spiritus est qui vivificat
pass_a_gloss: (4) Because carnal or corporal Participation of Christ’s body or flesh is expressly declared by Christ to be of no use at all, when with disciples still murmuring and not even then transmitting without indignation the word that seemed hard a little earlier, He at last about to put an end to more stubborn murmuring and bolt the door answers at v. 63: It is the Spirit that quickens, the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit and life … Augustine and Paschasius: without the Holy Spirit as Christ’s flesh profits nothing, so neither can this Sacrament of Christ profit … Brentius: flesh of Christ eaten as the Capernaites understood, torn with teeth, profits nothing; but profits much received by the mystery of faith and the teeth of the heart.
pass_b_english: (4) Carnal or corporal participation of Christ’s flesh is of no use at all (John 6:63): the Spirit quickens; the flesh profits nothing; His words are spirit and life.

Augustine and Paschasius: without the Spirit neither flesh nor sacrament profits; Lutherans admit Christ without faith harms; Brentius: Capernaite tooth-tearing profits nothing — faith’s heart-teeth do.
source_text: (4) Quia Carnalis seu Corporalis corporis aut carnis Christi Participatio nulli omnino usui esse disertè à Christo perhibetur, quando murmurantibus adhuc Discipulis & sibi durum paulò antè visum verbum nec tum quidem absque indignatione transmittentibus, ipse tandem pertinaciori obmurmurationi finem impositurus & pessulum obditurus vers. 63. respondet: Spiritus est qui vivificat, caro non prodest quicquam. Verba quæ ego loquor vobis, spiritus & vita sunt; Hisce verbis, vel binâ ratione expressa, Carnalem Præsentiam ac Participationem Carnis & Sanguinis sui suppressurus, erectis & in apricum positis solis Spiritualibus: primò quidem, dum carnem suam, non equidem per se spectatam, sed carnaliter manducandam (de qua sola hactenus disputatio, se inter & Judæos partim, partim Christianos discipulos suos, intercesserat) nihil prodesse ait, interpretante sic verba Augustino, Serm. secundô de Verbis Domini & suffragante Paschasio: Sine Spiritu S. inquit sicut nec caro Christi prodest quicquam, ita nec hoc Sacramentum Christi prodesse potest lib. 3. de Corp. & Sangv. Christi, i. e. Corpus Christi non prodest quicquam, non per se, sed per accidens & aliud, quod impedit illius Operationem, ut ipsi Lutherani, Lutherô contra Carlstadium præeunte, non possunt non fateri, quia sine fide Christus & Evangelium non tantum nihil prosunt, sed nocent, sunt odor mortis & judicium Dei accelerant. Unde Brentius in Exegesi Johannis: Verum equidem est, ait, carnem Christi comesam, quomodo Capernaitæ intellexerunt, dentibus laceratam, nihil prodesse, prodest autem plurimùm mysterio fidei & dentibus cordis accepta.
